"I want you to create a game about being a gritty, hard-boiled 1940s noir detective solving randomized murder mysteries late at night. 

Here is how the game works and what you need to build:
- Visuals @COMMENT_BODY@ Atmosphere: Dark, moody noir aesthetic with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting. Keep all text descriptions short, punchy, and under two sentences—no long paragraphs.
- Randomized Cases: Every time a new game starts, randomly generate a new Victim, a Murder Weapon, 3 Suspects (with motives and alibis), 4 Clues (including 1 definitive \"Smoking Gun\" clue that proves who did it), and 1 True Killer.
- Stage 1 - The Call: Start the game in a dark detective office with a rotary phone ringing at 2:00 AM. Give the player the crime scene address and a short tip from Sergeant Miller, with a button to [Head to the Crime Scene].
- Stage 2 - Top-Down Crime Scene: Show a top-down view of the crime scene room with 4 clickable/tappable objects (such as a desk, a shattered window, a coat, or a safe).
- Stage 3 - The Zoom-In: When the player taps an object, zoom in to a detailed close-up view of that object and reveal one clue with a single gritty sentence describing what was found. Include a button to [Zoom Out].
- Stage 4 - The Evidence Board: Always show a button to [Open Evidence Board]. On the Evidence Board screen, display all clues discovered so far, profile cards for the 3 suspects, and buttons to [Accuse a Suspect] or [Return to Crime Scene].
- Win/Loss Conditions: If the player accuses the wrong suspect, or tries to accuse the right suspect without having found the \"Smoking Gun\" clue first, trigger a Game Over screen where the killer escapes and the case goes cold. If the player finds the \"Smoking Gun\" and accuses the true killer, trigger a Victory screen where the killer is arrested.

Make sure the game is specifically designed for vertical mobile not pc, so no scrolling

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Need showScreen called after render for board/accuse. Important transitions: `.screen` transition with visibility .5s. On show, content. Fine. `renderCase` updates all IDs: ``` $('#officeCaseNo').textContent = `#${id}`; $('#millerLine').textContent = `“${tip}”`; ... ``` Scene victim: `${victim.name}` plus maybe role in sub. I have HUD sub "VICTIM — ". Set b to "Arthur Vale, nightclub owner". At 8px, could be long but max-width 230 ellipsis. Fine. Scene place: location.name. boardVictim name; boardVictimRole role. accuseCaseNo, boardCaseNo, sceneCaseNo, endCaseNo. - sceneArt.dataset.place. `renderSceneState`: ``` $$('.hotspot').forEach(btn=>{ const key = btn.dataset.object; const found = state.found.has(key); btn.classList.toggle('found',found); btn.querySelector('.tag').textContent = found ? `${OBJECTS[key].short} ✓` : OBJECTS[key].short; btn.setAttribute('aria-label', `${found?'Review':'Inspect'} ${OBJECTS[key].name}`); }); $('#clueProgress').textContent = `${state.found.size} OF 4 CLUES LOGGED`; ``` Maybe when 0 use "0 OF 4 CLUES LOGGED". Yes. Show a hint "4 OF 4 · OPEN THE BOARD" when all found? Clue progress could be. Keep. `openObject`: ``` const first = !state.found.has(key); state.currentObject=key; state.found.add(key); renderZoom(); showScreen('zoom'); if(first){ flash(); Sfx.clue(letter?); } ``` Flash via function: ``` function cameraFlash(){const f=$('#flash'); f.classList.remove('on'); void f.offsetWidth; f.classList.add('on');} ``` Sfx clue if enabled. `renderZoom`: - guard currentObject. - `clue` from caseData. - set text. - `clueSheet.classList.toggle('is-gun', type==='gun')` - gunTag hidden by CSS. - Set zoomCanvas innerHTML. Add closeup SVG. The art uses IDs; only one at a time. - set object labels. - `zoomFound` `${found.size} / 4`. - Set `zoomExhibit`: `EXHIBIT ${obj.exhibit} · ${obj.short}`. - plate. - Set `zoomArt.dataset.object`. - `#zoomArt` has `aria-label`? Set. - also log small status. - View: class .is-gun. `renderBoard`: Build HTML. Use tilt array based on object index: [-.35,.25,-.15,.4]. `--tilt`. Use `--i`. Locked cards show `CLUE 01 · DESK` and "NOT YET LOGGED — INSPECT THE {short}" maybe. Keep text "NOT YET LOGGED". Maybe "CLUE NOT YET LOGGED". Remember requirement 4 clues including gun; board shows all slots locked. - Escaping text via esc. - suspect portraits. - Suspect row maybe add no data; board list display. Fine. - If clues found, gun card red tag. `renderAccuse`: - state.selected reset when entering? It persists maybe. Set null each time to force deliberate selection. Yes renderAccuse sets state.selected=null unless passed preserve? On entering from board, reset. On clicking back from confirm, preserve. We call renderAccuse on entering; don't call when selecting. So set state.selected = null at render. Good. - HTML rows. - update button & warning after. - `setSelected(index)` updates classes, button disabled, text; ensure no re-render. - Make accusation opens confirm; if selected. - Do accuse evaluate: ``` const correct = state.selected === caseData.killerIndex; const hasGun = ...; const win = correct && hasGun; showEnd(win, {correct, hasGun}); ``` - `state.failure = !correct ? 'wrong' : !hasGun ? 'no-gun' : null`. `showEnd`: Detailed set. Classes on `#screen-end`. ``` end.classList.toggle('is-win', win); ... endStamp.textContent = win?'CASE CLOSED':'CASE COLD'; endHeadline = win?'The bracelets clicked.':'The killer walked.'; endCopy = ... endKillerLabel ... endKiller ... endVictim = `${victim.name} — ${victim.role}` maybe em dash; endWeapon = `a ${weapon}`; endNail.innerHTML = `THE NAIL ${esc(gun.text)}`; // text under 2 sentences ... showScreen('end') cameraFlash on win ``` For loss no gun: copy "You had the right name and empty hands. {killer} walked before the ink was dry." 2 sentences. For wrong: "The wrong name bought {killer} a clean getaway. By dawn, the trail was rain." Actually if wrong, the true killer is revealed but "the wrong name bought ..." nice. Win copy: "{killer} didn't say a word on the ride downtown. The city can sleep—for one night." 2 sentences. Hmm gritty. Good. Headline maybe "The bracelets clicked." nice. End weather text. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each new case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a definitive smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Gameplay stages: 2:00 AM phone call, top-down scene with four inspectable objects, close-up clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Accusing incorrectly or accusing before finding the smoking gun loses; correctly accusing after finding it wins.
- Designed for vertical mobile with no scrolling.

## Decisions
- Built from scratch as a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Added optional user-enabled synthesized rain/phone audio; no external runtime dependencies.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented randomized cases, four interactive objects/clues, evidence board, suspect accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Built noir office, crime-scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views with mobile-focused styling.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Improve the office scene, lamp, and phone, and make the phone ring, answer on tap, and lead into sergeant dialogue.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office should look better; lamp and phone should be visually improved.
- Phone must ring, be tappable to pick up, then display the sergeant's dialogue lines.
- Ringing sound should be better and remain optional/user-enabled.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Office call is now interactive and gated: the scene button stays disabled until the phone is answered and Miller's dialogue/address is completed.
- Phone is a real accessible button; office content uses `pointer-events:none` with interactive children re-enabled so taps reach the phone.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- End-screen booking-portrait card styling and short-screen variants.
- Fixed `.device`/`.screen` internal focus scrolling by using `overflow:clip`, preventing clipped screens.
- Upgraded office visuals: wall treatment, window mullions/droplets/sill, richer desk, dust motes, and lamp glow.
- Replaced the lamp with a detailed SVG banker's lamp with brass frame, base, pull chain, and warm bulb glow.
- Replaced the phone with a detailed SVG rotary phone: dial, numbers, handset, cord, highlights, and shadow.
- Added ringing animation, ring arcs, `TAP TO ANSWER` hint, and handset pickup animation.
- Added `state.call` plus `buildCallLines`, `resetCall`, `renderCallLine`, `answerPhone`, `finishCall`, and `advanceCall`.
- Added three sequential Miller dialogue lines, line counter, `NEXT`/`TAKE THE ADDRESS` action, address reveal, and updated clock/kicker.
- Improved synthesized ring with metallic bell partials, tremolo, and clapper click; added pickup thunk/static.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and full Playwright flows at `390×844`, `360×640`, and `320×568`, including win path, call reset, no-scroll layout, and audio enable/disable.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Office markup, phone/lamp SVGs, call dialogue card, other game screens.
- `game.js`: Case generation, call state/flow, audio synthesis, clue/board/accusation logic.
- `styles.css`: Office/noir artwork, phone/lamp styling, responsive layout, end-screen cards.
- `fonts/`: Locally bundled fonts used throughout the game.

## Important Context
- All current changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was made.
- Key office IDs: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.
- Call state lives in `state.call` as `{ answered, index, done, lines }`.
- `Sfx.startRing()` is gated by `state.call.answered`; toggling sound on after answering must not restart ringing.
- On short screens, answered state shifts `.office-lamp` and `.phone-zone` upward to keep them above the taller dialogue card.

content.text:
The office scene is now fully upgraded and the phone call is a real interactive beat. Here's what changed:

**Office artwork**
- Richer wall: warm lamp spill, panel seams, grime overlay, drifting dust motes.
- Window rebuilt with mullions, rain droplets, a sill, and cast blind shadows.
- Desk deepened with a wood-grain top, leather blotter, case file, and ashtray.

**Lamp**
- Replaced the flat shape with a detailed SVG banker's lamp: brass base, twin brass arms, crossbar, pull chain with bead, ribbed green glass shade, warm bulb bloom, and a soft breathing glow.

**Phone**
- Replaced with a detailed SVG rotary phone: gradient bakelite body, metal-rimmed dial with numbers and finger stop, coiled cord, handset holes, sheen, and drop shadow.
- It shakes and emits ring arcs while ringing, shows a pulsing `TAP TO ANSWER` tag, and the handset lifts when answered.

**Call flow**
- The phone is a real accessible button. Tapping it stops the ring, plays a pickup thunk/static, and reveals Sgt. Miller's dialogue card.
- Three sequential lines advance with `NEXT`; the last becomes `TAKE THE ADDRESS`, which reveals the crime-scene address and unlocks the scene button.
- Clock/kicker progress 02:00 → 02:02 → 02:05, and the whole call resets cleanly on a new case.

**Ring sound**
- Multi-partial metallic bell (fundamental + upper partials), band-pass shaping, tremolo, and a clapper click, repeating every ~3.4s. Still off by default and only plays until answered.

**Verification**
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Playwright flows at `390×844`, `360×640`, and `320×568`: full win path, call reset, no-scroll layout at every screen, and sound toggle (enabling after answering does not restart ringing).

All three files (`game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`) are modified but uncommitted.
